why: Modules are nodes and [a, b] is an edge b -> a (b compiles first). Kahn's algorithm with a min-heap of ready module names gives the deterministic order; if some modules never become ready, the dependencies contain a cycle.
hints: Which modules can compile right away, and what changes after one of them compiles?
Kahn's algorithm: in-degree = number of uncompiled prerequisites. The tie rule (smallest name first) means the ready set should be a min-heap of strings.
Map each name to its successors and in-degree; heap all in-degree-0 names; pop, append, decrement successors. If fewer than len(modules) come out, return ['IMPOSSIBLE']. O((V + E) log V).
pitfalls: [a, b] means a depends on b, so the edge points b -> a.
Modules with no dependencies at all still belong in the order.
